decision: Retain native floating-point GEE concentrations without a second 0.1 multiplier
verification_kind: Convergent source-format and magnitude audit, not byte-for-byte reproduction of the restricted V1 NetCDF
evidence: GEE V1 annual and daily assets contain floating-point concentrations at 0.1 microgram/m3 precision rather than unscaled integer packing values.

Open publisher V2 NetCDF uses uint16 with CF scale_factor 0.1 and units micrograms/m3. The publisher Python converter reads netCDF4 variables with automatic scale decoding and writes Float32 GeoTIFF values without another multiplier.
Raw GEE V1 annual values and its mean daily values agree to rounding at geographically separated points.

Decoded publisher V2 values at study, Johannesburg, Beijing and Delhi locations have the same concentration scale as unmultiplied GEE V1. V2 is a different release and is not treated as identical ground truth.
The original publication source-data archive reports concentrations in the same magnitude range, e.g. 2022 January 1 values of 43.25064 for China and 58.015694 for India (Figure 3).

The unmultiplied V1 GEE daily product was matched at the same date and coordinates to the original paper Figure 2 public monitor measurements; applying 0.1 greatly worsened scale consistency. This check does not establish independent predictive accuracy.
conflicting_metadata: The community catalog and example apply 0.1 to the already floating-point GEE assets. Following that example would reduce all estimates tenfold; this study does not apply that additional factor.
restriction: Original V1 Zenodo files require access as of this retrieval. No restricted files were accessed or bypassed.
version_separation: V1 GEE is the analysis series. Open V2 is used only in this unit audit; its values and coordinates are not mixed into V1 exposure results.

same_day_original_publication_check.purpose: Source-publication same-date unit consistency only; sites may overlap source training and are not local independent validation
